channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Iran submits 14-point response to U.S. proposal to end war
item.description: Iran submitted a 14-point response to the US proposal to end the war, according to Iranian state media. The response was presented to the US. Iran has presented a 14-point response to the U. S.

item.title: Trump says he is reviewing a new Iranian proposal to end the war
item.description: Trump is reviewing a new Iranian proposal to end the war. Details of the proposal are not available. Trump says he is reviewing a new Iranian proposal to end the war.

item.title: What to Know About the U.S.-Iran Peace Talks
item.description: Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz impasse stall war negotiations. Negotiations to end the war are at an impasse over Iran’s nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz, which remains mostly shut.

item.title: Trump says US could restart Iran strikes 'if they misbehave'
item.description: Trump said the US could restart Iran strikes if they misbehave. He doubts Iran's proposals will be acceptable. Trump also said that he could not imagine Iran's proposals would be acceptable and that Tehran had not paid a big enough price for what it had done.

item.title: The Iran war has strengthened Ukraine in surprising ways. Could a ceasefire with Russia be closer?
item.description: The Iran war strengthened Ukraine in unexpected ways. A ceasefire with Russia may be closer due to this development. The Iran war has strengthened Ukraine in surprising ways. Could a ceasefire with Russia be closer?

item.title: Germany says US troop withdrawal 'foreseeable' as Nato seeks clarification
item.description: Germany says a US troop withdrawal is foreseeable as Nato seeks clarification on the decision to pull out 5,000 troops. In the US, two senior Republicans voice concern over President Trump's decision to pull out 5,000 troops.

item.title: Germany says US troop drawdown should spur Europe, but top Republicans worried
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced a significant troop drawdown in Germany, stating he will cut more than 5,000 troops. Top Republicans expressed concern over the move, citing potential security implications for Europe. The exact timeline for the drawdown remains unclear.

item.title: Trump tells Congress ceasefire means he does not need their approval for Iran war
item.description: US President Donald Trump declared a ceasefire in hostilities with Iran, claiming congressional approval is no longer necessary. He argued that the ceasefire terminates hostilities, rendering congressional authorization unnecessary. The move has sparked debate over presidential authority.

item.title: U.S., Iran at odds on peace deal as Israel continues strikes on southern Lebanon
item.description: The US and Iran remain at odds over a peace deal, despite a ceasefire. Israel continues to strike targets in southern Lebanon, further straining regional tensions. The situation remains volatile, with no clear resolution in sight.

item.title: The rise of political violence under Trump
item.description: Professor Robert Pape attributes the rise of political violence in the US to President Trump's rhetoric and policies. Pape's research suggests a correlation between Trump's words and actions and increased violence. The professor's findings have sparked debate over the president's impact on national discourse.

item.title: ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric warns of the war's impact on civilians
item.description: ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric warned of the devastating impact of the Iran war on civilians during a recent visit to the country. She highlighted the humanitarian crisis unfolding in Iran, where civilians are bearing the brunt of the conflict.

item.title: US Supreme Court asked to restore abortion pill access
item.description: The US Supreme Court is asked to restore access to the abortion pill mifepristone. A lower court limited mail-order access. A lower court has limited mail-order access to the abortion pill mifepristone, which the drug's maker says will cause "irreparable harm".

item.title: Why are maritime laws failing to secure the seas?
item.description: Global shipping laws are being rewritten due to ongoing wars and territorial disputes. This shift is altering the rules that govern maritime security, with significant implications for the safety of shipping lanes.

item.title: Spirit Airlines collapses amid rising fuel costs from war on Iran
item.description: US budget carrier Spirit Airlines has shut down due to rising fuel costs. The airline's collapse comes after failed talks for a government bailout, leaving thousands of passengers stranded. US budget carrier Spirit Airlines shuts down after talks for a government bailout failed.

item.title: Why did the UAE quit OPEC and OPEC+?
item.description: The UAE has quit OPEC and OPEC+, citing simmering competition with Saudi Arabia. The move is expected to impact oil prices and may benefit India, although the full effects on the global energy market remain to be seen.

item.title: At least six dead in heavy rains in northeast Brazil, thousands displaced
item.description: Heavy rains in northeast Brazil have killed at least six people and displaced thousands. The extreme weather event has battered Pernambuco and Paraiba states, continuing a trend of increasingly frequent severe rain in the country.

item.title: Ukraine eyes Belarus border activities as Russian strikes persist
item.description: Ukraine monitors Belarus border activities as Russian strikes continue and sanctions are imposed. The role of Belarus in Russia's war on Ukraine has provoked sanctions from Kyiv, which says it is ready to respond.

item.title: Syria becomes alternative energy corridor for oil as Hormuz effectively blo
item.description: Syria receives hundreds of Iraqi oil trucks hauling crude overland as an alternative energy corridor to Europe. Syria is receiving hundreds of Iraqi oil trucks hauling crude overland as an alternative energy corridor to Europe.

item.title: Police arrest suspect over poisoned HiPP baby food
item.description: Austrian police arrested a 39-year-old man for allegedly attempting to blackmail a German baby food manufacturer over poisoned HiPP baby food. The suspect's involvement is still under investigation. A 39-year-old man has been arrested in Austria for his alleged involvement in an attempt to blackmail a German baby food manufacturer.
